title: Florida House, District 20
what_it_does: Represents District 20 (Putnam, Parts of Clay, Marion, St. Johns) in the Florida House; votes on state laws and the state budget.
verified_ballot_note: Candidate list taken from the Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list on 2026-09-18 (https://dos.elections.myflorida.com/candidates/CanList.asp); statuses Qualified/Unopposed only. Counties from the Legislature's district listings. Positions have not been researched yet.

candidates.name: Judson Sapp
candidates.photo_source: Ballotpedia candidate photo (downloaded copy in assets/photos)
candidates.occupation: CEO, W.J. Sapp Railroad Contractor; state representative (elected 2024)
candidates.background: Raised in Putnam County and an Eagle Scout, Sapp holds a philosophy degree from Florida State University and runs W.J. Sapp Railroad Contractor, a rail construction firm. He was elected to the Florida House in 2024 and lives in Green Cove Springs with his wife and two children.

roster_sources.title: Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list

property_tax.summary: Sapp says repealing property taxes is the top concern in his district and calls himself a believer in abolishing the tax, while suggesting a phased approach. He voted for HJR 203, the House plan to phase out non-school homestead property taxes, and was recorded as a 'yes' after the roll call on HJR 1F.
property_tax.quote: I would love it to be on the next ballot, and I hope it is, but you want us to do it right.

sources.title: Rep. Judson Sapp doubles down on property tax repeal push (Florida's Voice)
Floor Vote for CS/CS/HJR 203, Elimination of Non-school Property Taxes for Homesteads, Florida House
Floor Vote for CS/HJR 1F, Save Our Homes from Excessive Property Taxes (2026 special session), Florida House

immigration.summary: Voted for SB 2-C in the February 2025 special session, which created a State Board of Immigration Enforcement, required state and local cooperation with federal immigration enforcement and added state penalties for people in the country illegally.

sources.title: Floor Vote for SB 2-C, Immigration (2025 special session), Florida House
SB 2-C (2025C) Immigration, bill detail, Florida House

guns.summary: Voted for HB 759 (2025) and HB 133 (2026), which would lower the minimum age to buy a rifle or shotgun from 21 to 18; both passed the House and died in the Senate.

sources.title: Floor Vote for HB 759, Minimum Age for Firearm Purchase or Transfer, Florida House
Floor Vote for HB 133, Minimum Age for Firearm Purchase or Transfer, Florida House
Florida House passes bill to lower the age to purchase a long gun to 18 years (Florida Phoenix)

record.item: Voted yes on HJR 203 (phase-out of non-school homestead property taxes), Feb. 19, 2026; recorded as a yes after the roll call on HJR 1F, June 2, 2026.

sources.title: Floor Vote for CS/CS/HJR 203, Elimination of Non-school Property Taxes for Homesteads, Florida House
Floor Vote for CS/HJR 1F, Save Our Homes from Excessive Property Taxes (2026 special session), Florida House

record.item: Did not complete the News4JAX 2026 voter-guide questionnaire.

candidates.name: Lee Butler
candidates.background: Lee Wesley Butler of Palatka serves in the U.S. Navy Reserves and holds a master's degree in strategic studies. He has no prior political experience and told News4JAX his campaign has no website or social media presence.

roster_sources.title: Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list

veterans.summary: Butler lists veterans' benefits reform as his top priority, citing federal bills such as the Love Lives On Act and the Major Richard Star Act to protect survivor benefits.
veterans.quote: specific, bipartisan House bills that directly fix gaps in federal care for our veterans and public servants

healthcare.summary: He supports letting first responders who retire early between ages 50 and 64 buy into Medicare, a modest expansion of the government's role in coverage.
healthcare.quote: allowing first responders between the ages of 50 and 64 who separate from service early to buy into Medicare

other_issues.title: Military leave for first responders
other_issues.summary: Supports requiring police and fire departments to provide up to 26 days of paid military leave, mirroring federal House Bills 5232 and 5233.
